content: Fluorine deficiency, also referred to as fluoride or fluorine deficiency, is a medical condition in which an individual or organism lacks sufficient fluorine-containing compounds necessary for maintaining the health of bones and teeth. The existence of this condition and its relationship to fluoride toxicity has been a subject of some controversy. The American Dental Hygiene Association considers fluoride to be essential for the development and maintenance of healthy teeth. The systemic effects of fluoride were first observed in 1931, when it was discovered that high concentrations of fluoride could stain teeth while simultaneously preventing tooth decay. However, excessive fluoride exposure has been scientifically linked to severe health issues, including death, brain damage, hypothyroidism, cancer, liver damage, impaired kidney function, and dental fluorosis in children. As a result, anti-fluoridation groups argue that exposing communities to fluoride poses unnecessary risks and should be avoided.
